name: Raw meat / raw liver diet

card.summary: Eating uncooked meat and organs for supposed growth-factor, skin and bone gains; no human trials exist, and documented infections are tied to raw liver and undercooked meat.
card.note: Case reports and reviews link raw liver and undercooked meat to parasitic and viral infections.

quick.overview:
The raw meat or raw liver diet is a variant of meat-based eating in which animal foods, including organs such as liver and heart, are eaten uncooked. On looksmax.org it is promoted by some members for supposed growth hormone and IGF-1 effects and skin or body benefits, and criticized by others.

No published human studies have tested it for appearance outcomes. The medical literature in this area is mostly case reports and reviews describing infections linked to raw liver and undercooked meat.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say raw animal foods retain nutrients that cooking degrades and boost natural IGF-1 and growth hormone production. No clinical study has tested these claims. Raw liver is a rich source of vitamins and minerals including preformed vitamin A.
quick.risks: Reviews and case reports link raw liver to Taenia asiatica tapeworm infection, fascioliasis, toxoplasmosis, toxocariasis and halzoun syndrome, and undercooked pork products to hepatitis E. Wikipedia reports that a single slice of beef liver can exceed the tolerable upper intake for preformed vitamin A, and that thorough cooking kills parasites, viruses and most bacteria.

lead: The raw meat or raw liver diet involves eating meat, organs and often dairy uncooked. One looksmax.org member describing his plan listed raw milk products, raw organs such as liver, hearts and bones, raw meat and fish, and occasional fruit with no vegetables, citing natural IGF-1 production, increased growth hormone and skin endurance as expected benefits. [1]

Other members argue the approach is hype from TikTok and could affect health during puberty. [2] No published trials have examined raw meat or raw liver diets in people for appearance or health outcomes.

The medical literature documents infections tied to raw liver and undercooked meat, including tapeworm in Taiwanese communities that ate raw wild boar liver, toxoplasmosis outbreaks in Korea after raw pig liver or spleen, and halzoun syndrome from raw sheep liver in the Eastern Mediterranean. [3][4][5] Wikipedia reports that thorough cooking kills parasites, viruses and most bacteria. [6]
infobox: Raw meat, organs (liver, heart), sometimes raw dairy [1]

paras: The diet overlaps with carnivore and primal eating but specifies that animal foods be uneaten cooked, often with an emphasis on organ meats. [1] Raw liver appears in several traditional cuisines, for example Lebanese asbeh nayeh and Japanese liver sashimi, according to Wikipedia. [8]

Wikipedia reports that animal liver is rich in iron, copper, B vitamins and preformed vitamin A, and that a single 68 g slice of beef liver exceeds the tolerable upper intake for preformed vitamin A. [8]

No studies found of raw meat or raw liver diets in people. Related research is limited to infection reports and veterinary studies on raw feeding of cats, which are not evidence about human appearance or health. [9]

A historical review of Taenia asiatica in Taiwan attributes high tapeworm prevalence among aboriginal communities to a culture of eating raw liver from hunted wild boar. [3] Two Korean toxoplasmosis outbreaks followed meals of raw wild pig spleen and liver and raw domestic pig liver. [7] A case report and review of halzoun syndrome describes nasopharyngeal symptoms after raw sheep liver in the Eastern Mediterranean and advises counseling on the hazards of raw liver in endemic areas. [5]

A review of human fascioliasis lists raw liver ingestion among risk factors. [10] A familial case of visceral toxocariasis was linked to raw bovine liver. [11] Hepatitis E reviews state that infections occur through eating undercooked meat from pigs, boar and deer. [12] A French study found matching hepatitis E virus sequences in humans with locally acquired infection and in swine livers. [13]
Wikipedia notes that Salmonella, E. coli O157:H7 and Campylobacter are common bacterial causes of foodborne illness and that infants, young children and travelers are particularly vulnerable. [6]
Posts on looksmax.org range from members planning raw diets and documenting them, to a thread arguing raw meat is hype and may affect development during puberty. [1][2]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, raw meat diets are posted about as a primal approach to growth and skin, and are disputed by other members. [1][2]

claims.claim: Eating raw meat and organs boosts natural IGF-1 and growth hormone and improves skin.
claims.believers: A poster planning the diet lists natural IGF-1 production, increased GH and skin endurance as benefits and says he sources meat from a local farm. [1]
claims.experts: No published human studies have tested raw meat diets for IGF-1, growth hormone or skin outcomes.

claims.claim: Raw eating is safe if sourcing is good.
claims.believers: Members advise obtaining products from local farms rather than supermarkets. [1]
claims.experts: Case reports and reviews link raw liver and undercooked pork to tapeworm, toxoplasmosis, fascioliasis, toxocariasis and hepatitis E; Wikipedia states thorough cooking kills parasites, viruses and most bacteria. [3][6][7][12]

claims.claim: The diet is hype and affects development during puberty.
claims.believers: A poster argues raw meat and carnivore diets are overhyped on TikTok, and that cutting carbohydrates in puberty harms health. [2]
claims.experts: No published studies examined raw meat diets in adolescents.
